placeholder.title: Coming soon
placeholder.description: This section is part of a later milestone. The app shell is ready; the data will appear here once the agent is connected.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Changes apply immediately and are saved for your Windows user.
appearance.reduceMotionHint: Turns off pulses, arcs and transitions. Also enabled when Windows asks for reduced motion.

startup.title: Startup
startup.description: Choose whether PacketWard opens by itself.
startup.autostartHint: Opens minimized to the system tray when you sign in. The agent runs regardless.

language.title: Language
language.description: Automatic follows the Windows display language.
language.label: Interface language

about.title: About PacketWard
about.tagline: Network defense and diagnostics for Windows Server VPS and RDP machines.
about.madeBy: Built by XeroHost and released as open source.

notInstalled.title: The PacketWard agent is not installed
notInstalled.body: PacketWard needs its background service to watch your network, even while you are disconnected. Install it to continue.

stopped.title: The PacketWard agent is not running
stopped.body: The background service is installed but stopped, so nothing is being monitored. Start it to continue.

starting.title: Starting the PacketWard agent…
starting.body: This usually takes a few seconds.

groupMissing.title: Your account cannot reach the agent yet
groupMissing.body: The “PacketWard Operators” group does not exist. Repair the installation to create it and add your account.

notMember.title: Your account is not allowed to use the agent
notMember.body: Only administrators and members of the “PacketWard Operators” group can connect. Repair the installation to add your account.

signOutRequired.title: Sign out of Windows and sign back in
signOutRequired.body: Your account is in the “PacketWard Operators” group, but Windows only applies this when you sign in. Disconnecting and reconnecting Remote Desktop is not enough: sign out completely, then open PacketWard again.

unexplained.title: The agent refused the connection
unexplained.body: Your account looks allowed, yet access was denied. Try Repair; if it keeps happening, check the agent log in C:\ProgramData\PacketWard\logs.

agentOutdated.title: The agent is out of date
agentOutdated.body: The installed agent is older than this app and cannot communicate with it. Update PacketWard.

uiOutdated.title: This app is out of date
uiOutdated.body: The agent is newer than this app and cannot communicate with it. Update PacketWard.

error.title: Could not connect to the agent
error.body: Something unexpected stopped the connection. Repair can fix most cases.

unavailable.uacHint: Windows will ask for administrator permission.
unavailable.cancelled: The Windows permission prompt was declined, so nothing changed.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Live connection to the PacketWard agent service.

dashboard.oldAgent: The installed agent is older than this app and does not report traffic or connections. Update PacketWard.

tiles.connectionsHint: {total} in total · {waiting} waiting to close · {half} half-open

chart.title: Traffic, last 5 minutes
chart.empty: Waiting for data from the agent…

topRemote.title: Top remote addresses
topRemote.description: Who holds the most connections to this machine right now.

adapters.title: Network adapters
adapters.description: Only real adapters are added to the totals; tunnels and VPNs are shown apart.

rdp.title: Remote Desktop
rdp.description: Sessions on this machine and the addresses they connect from.
rdp.none: Nobody is connected through Remote Desktop.
rdp.peers: Connected to the RDP port from
rdp.note: These are addresses with an open connection to the RDP port. That includes anyone who has not signed in yet, so it is not proof of a legitimate session. The address a client reports for itself can differ (NAT, VPN).
rdp.trustedTitle: Addresses with a successful RDP logon (last {days} days)
rdp.trustedDescription: These are the addresses the Guardian will never block. A bot that only connects or fails to sign in never appears here.
rdp.trustedLoading: Reading recent logons from the event log…
rdp.trustedUnavailable: Cannot read the Security event log: no address can be learned.
rdp.trustedEmpty: No successful RDP logon found in the event log for this period.

connections.rdpBadgeTip: Has an open connection to the Remote Desktop port
connections.truncated: The agent sent only the first {n} rows to stay within its size limit.
connections.unsupported: The installed agent is older than this app and cannot provide the connection list. Update PacketWard.
connections.failed: Could not read the connection list from the agent. It will try again.
connections.rdpTrustedBadgeTip: Connected to the RDP port and has a successful RDP logon

audit.successOff: Windows is not auditing successful logons: PacketWard cannot learn which RDP clients are legitimate, so the Guardian could not protect them.
audit.successUnknown: The audit policy for successful logons could not be read: PacketWard cannot tell whether RDP logons are recorded.
audit.failureOff: Windows is not auditing failed logons: RDP brute-force attacks cannot be detected.
audit.failureUnknown: The audit policy for failed logons could not be read: RDP brute-force detection may not work.
audit.feedUnavailable: The Security event log cannot be read, so successful RDP logons are not being learned.
audit.howToFix: Turn both on from an administrator shell:

errors.notConnected: The agent is not connected. Start it and try again.
errors.unsupported: The installed agent is older than this app and does not provide diagnostics. Update the agent.
errors.busy: Too many diagnostics are running at once. Stop one and try again.

ping.hint: Sends ICMP echo requests to measure reachability, latency and jitter.

mtr.hint: Traces the route to a host and measures loss and latency at every router, like MTR. Use Copy report to send the result to support.
mtr.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
mtr.rateLimitedTip: Later hops are clean: this router probably only limits its ICMP replies.
mtr.rateLimitedNote: Loss here is not carried to the next hops, so this router is probably just rate-limiting its replies, not dropping traffic.

dns.hint: Looks up DNS records with the system resolver or a public one, to tell a DNS problem from a network problem.
dns.name: Name

port.hint: Tries to connect from this machine to a host and port. To test whether this server is reachable from outside, run the check from another machine.

explain.closed: The host answered and refused the connection: nothing is listening there.
explain.filtered: No answer at all. A firewall is probably dropping the traffic, or the host is down.
explain.inconclusive: UDP has no handshake: no reply does not prove the port is closed, nor open.

local.hint: What this machine is listening on. A port reachable from all interfaces is exposed to the network unless a firewall blocks it.
